intro_html: Peanut sauce makes almost anything taste like a treat, and this Thai-inspired bowl is no exception. It brings 63 grams of protein and a creamy coconut-peanut sauce for about $3.57 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one pot means you can eat like this all week and still come out ahead.
cost_closing_html: About $3.57 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: You get 63 grams of protein and 603 calories per serving, richer than the others but still a smart, filling plate.
upsell_html: Creamy, a little sweet, and cheap enough to keep on repeat. Hard combo to beat. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: That jar of peanut butter powers the whole sauce for under a dollar's worth, so the pantry staple you already own is doing the heavy lifting.
Canned coconut milk is far cheaper than the carton kind and keeps for a year, so buy a few cans at once.
Red peppers cost the most of any veg here, so watch for the three-pack sale and buy them when they're marked down.
make_it: Add the chicken, peanut butter, coconut milk, chicken broth, soy sauce, honey, and garlic to the slow cooker and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender and the sauce is glossy.
Stir in the sliced red bell pepper for the last 45 minutes so it softens but holds its shape.
Whisk the sauce smooth, then shred the chicken right back into it.
Serve over white rice and spoon extra sauce on top.
